ICE cotton futures edged lower as profit-booking followed a strong rally that had lifted prices to a two-month high.
Weaker crude oil prices also weighed on sentiment.
However, tightening ICE certified stocks, hot and dry weather in the US, below-average monsoon forecasts in India, and expected lower output in Brazil continued to underpin the market, keeping the broader trend bullish.

summary:

Five initiatives span productivity monitoring, e-learning, startup incubation, Gen Z design and recycled defence textiles.

title: RBI keeps repo rate unchanged at 5.25%, retains neutral stance
summary:
The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee kept the repo rate unchanged at 5.25 per cent and retained its neutral stance, citing persistent inflation risks and global uncertainty. 
It projected 6.7 per cent GDP growth and 5.0 per cent CPI inflation for 2026-27, while highlighting food and fuel prices, monsoon conditions, geopolitics and global trade as key risks to the outlook.

title: US manufacturing hits 4-year high as exports rebound in July
summary:
US manufacturing activity surged in July at the strongest rate in more than four years, with the ISM PMI expanding for a seventh straight month.
New export orders returned to expansion, while production, payrolls and wages rose, signalling stronger demand for US-made goods.
Capital goods imports exceeded 40 per cent of US goods imports as factories retooled and expanded.

title: UK may face recession in H2 2026 if Strait of Hormuz stays closed: EY
summary:
Despite softening activity, underlying UK economic momentum was relatively robust in Q2 2026, helped by lower-than-expected inflation and falling global energy prices, EY said.
However, a return to full-blown conflict and an extended closure of the Strait could see UK inflation peak above 6 per cent and economic growth go into reverse before 2026 end, it said in in its ‘UK Economic Outlook Summer 2026’.

title: Who's really buying China's clothes? Inside the domestic fashion boom
summary:
China’s garment, footwear, headwear and knitted textile retail sales topped 1.5 trillion yuan in 2025, up 3.2 per cent, as exports fell 2.4 per cent.
Domestic apparel brands raised share from 35.8 per cent in 2020 to 56.1 per cent by 2024, with guochao demand behind the shift.
Gen Z, social commerce, AI-personalised recommendations, athleisure and livestreams are reshaping apparel e-commerce.

title: Turkey's cost pressure accelerates Egypt's garment rise
summary:
Eastern Mediterranean apparel sourcing is shifting as Egypt gains momentum.
TexPro US customs data show US imports of Egyptian knitted apparel rose 48.4 per cent year on year to $78.5 million in May 2026, while woven apparel increased 58.4 per cent to $44.3 million.
Although Türkiye's shipments also grew, rising domestic production costs are strengthening Egypt's competitive position.

title: Guangdong, Zhejiang, Jiangsu: Inside China's three-way textile rivalry
summary:
China's textile and apparel exports totalled $293.77 billion in 2025, with Guangdong, Zhejiang and Jiangsu accounting for 70–80 per cent of output.
Zhejiang leads by revenue and export value, built on synthetic fibre, fabric trading, Yiwu distribution and digital/smart factories.
Jiangsu's vertical chain and Guangdong's finished-garment base show competition shifting from cost to capability.

title: Sri Lankan garment exports reach $2.2 bn in H1 2026
summary:
Sri Lanka’s garment exports fell 5.8 per cent to $2,264.1 million in January-June 2026, from $2,403.3 million a year earlier. 
Textile exports also declined 5.8 per cent to $134.0 million, while other manufactured textile articles dropped 12.4 per cent to $52.9 million. 
The sector still made up 45.18 per cent of industrial exports, keeping apparel central to sourcing exposure.

title: Bangladesh’s BGMEA calls media reports of RMG units’ closure baseless
summary:
Bangladesh trade body BGMEA has dismissed claims by some media outlets that several garment factories, including those of the DBL Group, were shut down due to gas and power shortage.  
Terming the information as ‘completely false and baseless’, it said despite gas and power shortage, BGMEA member factories have managed to keep their production activities operational with government support.

title: Europe powered 67% of Egypt’s apparel export growth
summary:
Egypt’s apparel exports rose 15 per cent to $1.775 billion in H1 2026, with Europe delivering about 67 per cent of the net gain.
Europe and the US supplied 82.3 per cent of shipments, exposing exporters to market and product concentration.
TexPro data point to woven demand in Europe, knitted growth in the US, and higher EU compliance pressure from July 19, 2026.

title: Japan's Yonex begins renewable solar power use at Niigata factory
summary:
Yonex has begun using renewable solar energy at its Niigata Factory Nagaoka through an on-site PPA.  The 896.72 kW system is expected to generate about 850,000 kWh annually and cut CO₂ emissions by around 295 tons. 
The initiative supports Yonex’s Carbon Neutrality goals and expands its use of renewable energy across manufacturing sites.

title: India’s Raymond Lifestyle’s Q1 earnings grow 11%; garmenting jumps 50%
summary:
Raymond Lifestyle has reported a stable Q1 FY27, with total income rising 6 per cent YoY to ₹1,560 crore (~$163.7 million) and EBITDA up 11 per cent to ₹135 crore (~$14.17 million). 
Strong garmenting growth, driven by export demand and trade tailwinds, offset softer textile performance. 
The company also strengthened its balance sheet, ending the quarter with a net cash position.

title: Bangladesh can unlock $5 bn apparel exports with plastic recycling
summary:
Bangladesh could add $4-5 billion in apparel exports by scaling plastic-to-textile recycling, BUILD has estimated. 
The push targets lower reliance on imported man-made fibres and alignment with European Union's circularity requirements. 
Policy proposals include a circular economy policy, better collection, traceability, recycled PET standards and certification.

title: Albania’s apparel exports grow 36% in Jan-April, momentum continues
summary:
Albania’s apparel exports rose 36.8 per cent year on year to $193.19 million in January-April 2026, TexPro data showed.
Nearshoring demand from European fashion buyers lifted CMT-led orders as brands sought shorter lead times and sourcing flexibility.
Imports more than doubled to $156.25 million, indicating higher inward processing for re-export rather than domestic demand.
